```
/// Compete every jet-admitted surface type from one seed face and return the
/// winner: the hypothesis with the **largest validated area**, simplest-DOF
/// tiebreak, after the \`MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG\` identifiability guard.
///
/// This is the whole of \`compete_region\`'s per-seed work, extracted verbatim so
/// that the invariant harness (\`super::invariants\`) drives the *same* code the
/// pipeline does rather than a reimplementation of it. \`compete_region\` keeps
/// ownership of seed ordering, claiming and resolution.
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
pub(super) fn compete_from_seed(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    seed: usize,
    jet: &[JetField],
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
    flat_eps: f64,
    debug: bool,
) -> Option<(CompeteHyp, f64, u8)> {
    {
        let jf = jet[seed];
        // Dominant / secondary principal-curvature MAGNITUDES. The jet orders
        // k1 ≥ k2 by signed value, so for a concave feature (a hole wall,
        // κ = −1/r) the dominant curvature is negative and lands in k2 —
        // taking |k1| as the dominant would read the wall's flat axial
        // direction and treat the hole as planar. Order by magnitude instead.
        let a1 = jf.k1.abs().max(jf.k2.abs());
        let a2 = jf.k1.abs().min(jf.k2.abs());

        // Grow the jet-pruned candidate types; keep the largest validated
        // area (simplest-DOF tiebreak).
        let mut best: Option<(CompeteHyp, f64, u8)> = None; // (hyp, area, dof)
        let consider = |hyp_area: Option<(CompeteHyp, f64)>, dof: u8, best: &mut Option<(CompeteHyp, f64, u8)>| {
            if let Some((h, area)) = hyp_area {
                let sweep = candidate_sweep(mesh, &h);
                if sweep < MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG.to_radians() {
                    if debug {
                        eprintln!(
                            "    compete: seed {seed} rejected {} sweeping only {:.1}\u{00b0} about its axis — radius undetermined ({} faces, area {area:.2})",
                            h.kind_name(),
                            sweep.to_degrees(),
                            h.faces().len(),
                        );
                    }
                    return;
                }
                let better = match best {
                    None => true,
                    Some((_, ba, bd)) => area > *ba + 1e-9 || ((area - *ba).abs() <= 1e-9 && dof < *bd),
                };
                if better {
                    *best = Some((h, area, dof));
                }
            }
        };

        // Plane is always a candidate (cheap; catches misread flats).
        let plane = grow::<PlanarSurface>(mesh, in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, 1);
        let mut cone_area = None;
        let mut sphere_area = None;
        let mut torus_area = None;
        if a1 >= flat_eps {
            // Curved: a developable (cylinder/cone) is always plausible.
            let cone = grow::<ConicalSurface>(mesh, in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, MIN_CYLINDER_FACES);
            cone_area = cone.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));

            // Toroidal candidate: a direct grow from this seed (fillet tori,
            // bend tubes), skipped when the seed reads sphere-like — every
            // adjacent quad-row band of a sphere lies near some torus, so a
            // (κ,κ) seed's torus is at best a bogus band that loses to the
            // sphere anyway. A torus seed reads |κ2| < |κ1| (κ2 varies
            // azimuthally around the tube; it only approaches κ1 near the
            // degenerate R≈r hole of a donut — a whole-region ladder case,
            // not a competition case).
            let mut torus = if a2 < 0.8 * a1 {
                let patch = seed_patch(mesh, in_region, seed, jet);
                torus_candidate(mesh, in_region, &patch, &[seed], centroids, config)
            } else {
                None
            };
            // Bent-tube promotion: a cylinder that stalled against
            // tube-continuation faces is the developable prefix of a bent
            // tube; grow a torus from the pure-bend patch past the stall.
            if let Some((cyl, _, cyl_faces)) = cone.as_ref() {
                if cyl.is_cylinder() {
                    let promoted =
                        promote_bend(mesh, in_region, cyl, cyl_faces, jet, centroids, config);
                    if let Some(p) = promoted {
                        if torus.as_ref().is_none_or(|(_, a, _)| p.1 > *a) {
                            torus = Some(p);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            torus_area = torus.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));

            consider(cone.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Conical(h), a)), 2, &mut best);
            // Curved in both directions → also try a sphere.
            if a2 >= 0.3 * a1 {
                let sphere = grow::<SphericalSurface>(mesh, in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, MIN_SPHERE_FACES);
                sphere_area = sphere.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));
                consider(sphere.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Spherical(h), a)), 1, &mut best);
            }
            consider(torus.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Toroidal(h), a)), 3, &mut best);
        }
        let plane_area = plane.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));
        consider(plane.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Planar(h), a)), 0, &mut best);

        if debug && best.is_none() {
            eprintln!(
                "    compete: seed {seed} jet=({:.3},{:.3}) class {:?} → NO GROWTH (plane {plane_area:?} cone {cone_area:?} sphere {sphere_area:?} torus {torus_area:?})",
                jf.k1, jf.k2, curvature_class(jf),
            );
        }

        if let Some((hyp, area, dof)) = best.as_ref() {
            if debug {
                eprintln!(
                    "    compete: seed {seed} → {} ({} faces, area {area:.2}, dof {dof}, sweep {:.1}\u{00b0})",
                    hyp.kind_name(),
                    hyp.faces().len(),
                    match hyp {
                        CompeteHyp::Toroidal(t) => torus_sweep(mesh, t).to_degrees(),
                        CompeteHyp::Conical(c) => conical_sweep(mesh, c).to_degrees(),
                        _ => 0.0,
                    }
                );
            }
        }
        best
```

```
pub(super) fn compete_region(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    region: &Region,
    jet: &[JetField],
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
) -> (Vec<CompeteHyp>, Vec<usize>) {
    let n = mesh.faces.len();
    let debug = config.verbosity >= 3 || std::env::var("BREPPER_DEBUG_COMPETE").is_ok();
    let mut in_region = vec![false; n];
    for &fi in &region.faces {
        in_region[fi] = true;
    }
    // Region curvature scale: a face reads "flat" when its principal
    // curvature radius exceeds a couple of region diameters.
    let extent = region_extent(mesh, region);
    let flat_eps = if extent > 0.0 { 1.0 / (2.0 * extent) } else { 1e-6 };
    // Seed order: jet-interior-first (ascending curvature mismatch with
    // region neighbors), ties by face index for determinism.
    let mut seeds = region.faces.clone();
    let score: Vec<f64> = (0..n)
        .map(|fi| {
            if !in_region[fi] {
                return f64::INFINITY;
            }
            neighbor_jet_mismatch(mesh, fi, jet, &in_region)
        })
        .collect();
    seeds.sort_by(|&a, &b| {
        score[a]
            .partial_cmp(&score[b])
            .unwrap()
            .then_with(|| a.cmp(&b))
    });
    // Every region face seeds exactly once — \`seeds\` is a permutation of them,
    // which is what terminates the loop. Committing a hypothesis does NOT
    // remove the faces it grew into from the seed pool.
    //
    // Growing into a face is a hypothesis, not a conclusion. The committed
    // face set is always a \`flood\` output, so every member validates — but
    // against a fit whose parameters came from an unvalidated seed
    // neighbourhood, so "validated" does not mean "the right surface". Letting
    // those faces seed too means a wrong hypothesis can be out-competed by a
    // right one grown from a face it had swallowed; \`resolve_claims\` already
    // exists to arbitrate the multi-claims that produces.
    //
    // It also makes the long-standing claim that seed misordering "costs only
    // time" actually true: previously an early bad hypothesis consumed faces a
    // later, better seed needed.
    let mut committed: Vec<CompeteHyp> = Vec::new();
    let mut claim_lists: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); n]; // face -> committed idxs
    let mut claimed = vec![false; n];
    for &seed in &seeds {
        // Skip only faces in the INTERIOR of what is already explained: every
        // neighbour claimed too. Seeding there cannot produce a competitor —
        // a fit grown from the middle of a validated surface refits that same
        // surface — so it is pure cost. Faces at the margin still seed.
        if claimed[seed] && interior_of_claims(mesh, seed, &claimed) {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some((hyp, _area, _dof)) =
            compete_from_seed(mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, flat_eps, debug)
        {
            let idx = committed.len();
            for &f in hyp.faces() {
                claim_lists[f].push(idx);
                claimed[f] = true;
            }
            committed.push(hyp);
        }
        // A seed that grows nothing analytic costs only its own turn.
    }
    resolve_claims(
        mesh,
        &region.faces,
        &mut committed,
        &claim_lists,
        config.vertex_tolerance_mm,
        config,
    )
}
```

<summary>Bash: Make the fit memo shareable across threads</summary>

```bash
grep -rn "thread_local!\|static mut\|static .*RefCell\|static .*Cell<" src/stage2/ | head; python3 - <<'PY'
p='src/stage2/surface.rs'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("    type Fit: Clone + 'static;","    type Fit: Clone + Send + 'static;",1)
old_start=s.find('/// Cache key: the surface type and its exact fit inputs.')
old_end=s.find('/// `S::fit_surface`, memoized while')
new_mid='''/// Cache key: the surface type and its exact fit inputs.
type FitKey = (std::any::TypeId, Vec<usize>, Vec<usize>);
type FitMap = std::collections::HashMap<FitKey, Box<dyn std::any::Any + Send>>;

/// One stage-2 run's fit memo, shared by every thread working on that run.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(super) struct FitCache(std::sync::Arc<std::sync::Mutex<FitMap>>);

thread_local! {
    /// The memo this thread fills and reads, while one is installed.
    static FIT_CACHE: std::cell::RefCell<Option<FitCache>> = const { std::cell::RefCell::new(None) };
}

/// Install `cache` on this thread for the duration of `f` (also on panic).
fn with_installed<R>(cache: Option<FitCache>, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R {
    struct Restore(Option<FitCache>);
    impl Drop for Restore {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let prev = self.0.take();
            FIT_CACHE.with(|c| *c.borrow_mut() = prev);
        }
    }
    let prev = FIT_CACHE.with(|c| c.replace(cache));
    let _restore = Restore(prev);
    f()
}

/// Run `f` with a fresh fit memo installed on this thread (if `enabled`), and
/// drop it afterwards.
///
/// **Why it is safe:** `fit_surface` is a deterministic function of the mesh,
/// the face list and the vertex list (verbosity only gates printing), and the
/// mesh is borrowed immutably for the whole of stage 2.3–2.4. So a stored fit
/// for an identical `(type, faces, vertices)` key is exactly what recomputing
/// would return — every result is bit-identical, whichever thread computed it.
/// The memo is scoped to one stage-2 run so face indices from different meshes
/// can never collide.
///
/// **Why it pays:** competition reaches the same patch from different seeds and
/// flood starts. Measured with a probe, repeated torus fits were 33 s of
/// `rounded_cube_10_r2_fine`'s 68 s of torus fitting and 30 s of
/// `pipe_elbow_10_fine`'s 124 s.
pub(super) fn with_fit_cache<R>(enabled: bool, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R {
    let cache = enabled.then(|| FitCache(Default::default()));
    with_installed(cache, f)
}

/// The memo installed on this thread, to hand to worker threads.
pub(super) fn current_fit_cache() -> Option<FitCache> {
    FIT_CACHE.with(|c| c.borrow().clone())
}

/// Run `f` on a worker thread with the run's memo (from [`current_fit_cache`]).
pub(super) fn with_shared_fit_cache<R>(cache: Option<FitCache>, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R {
    with_installed(cache, f)
}

'''

old_fn_start=s.find('/// `S::fit_surface`, memoized while')
new_fn='''/// `S::fit_surface`, memoized while a fit memo is installed and
/// `S::CACHE_FITS` is set; otherwise a plain call.
pub(super) fn cached_fit<S>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    face_list: &[usize],
    vertex_list: &[usize],
    verbosity: u8,
) -> Option<S::Fit>
where
    S: SurfaceType,
{
    if !S::CACHE_FITS {
        return S::fit_surface(mesh, face_list, vertex_list, verbosity);
    }
    let Some(cache) = current_fit_cache() else {
        return S::fit_surface(mesh, face_list, vertex_list, verbosity);
    };
    let key: FitKey = (std::any::TypeId::of::<S>(), face_list.to_vec(), vertex_list.to_vec());
    let hit = cache.0.lock().expect("fit memo").get(&key).map(|v| {
        v.downcast_ref::<Option<S::Fit>>().expect("keyed by type").clone()
    });
    if let Some(found) = hit {
        return found;
    }
    // Computed outside the lock, so threads never wait on each other's fits.
    // Two threads may compute the same key at once; they produce the same value.
    let fit = S::fit_surface(mesh, face_list, vertex_list, verbosity);
    cache.0.lock().expect("fit memo").insert(key, Box::new(fit.clone()));
    fit
}
'''
```

```bash
new='''    // Skip only faces in the INTERIOR of what is already explained: every
    // neighbour claimed too. Seeding there cannot produce a competitor — a fit
    // grown from the middle of a validated surface refits that same surface —
    // so it is pure cost. Faces at the margin still seed.
    let skip = |seed: usize, claimed: &[bool]| claimed[seed] && interior_of_claims(mesh, seed, claimed);
    let threads = competition_threads(debug);
    // Seeds are taken in blocks. Within a block every seed not already skipped
    // is evaluated — in parallel when `threads > 1` — and the results are then
    // applied strictly in seed order, re-checking the skip rule as claims grow.
    //
    // This is exactly the serial loop. `compete_from_seed` reads only the mesh,
    // the region and the seed, never the claims, so its result for a seed does
    // not depend on when it is computed; claims decide only WHETHER a seed is
    // used, and a seed used at its turn was necessarily unskipped at the start
    // of its block (claims only grow). A seed that becomes skipped mid-block
    // was computed for nothing and is discarded — the price of the
    // parallelism, small because a block is only a few seeds per thread.
    let block = if threads > 1 { threads * COMPETE_BLOCK_PER_THREAD } else { 1 };
    let cache = super::surface::current_fit_cache();
    let mut pos = 0;
    while pos < seeds.len() {
        let end = (pos + block).min(seeds.len());
        let todo: Vec<usize> = seeds[pos..end]
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|&s| !skip(s, &claimed))
            .collect();
        let mut results = evaluate_seeds(&todo, threads, cache.clone(), |seed| {
            compete_from_seed(mesh, &in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, flat_eps, debug)
        });
        for &seed in &seeds[pos..end] {
            if skip(seed, &claimed) {
                continue;
            }

                .remove(&seed)
                .expect("a seed unskipped at its turn was unskipped at its block's start");

                let idx = committed.len();
                for &f in hyp.faces() {
                    claim_lists[f].push(idx);
                    claimed[f] = true;
                }
                committed.push(hyp);
            }
            // A seed that grows nothing analytic costs only its own turn.
        }
        pos = end;

helpers='''
/// Seeds evaluated per thread per block in `compete_region`. Bounds the work a
/// block can waste on seeds that an earlier seed of the same block turns out to
/// cover; it never changes a result.
const COMPETE_BLOCK_PER_THREAD: usize = 2;

/// Worker threads for competition: 1 (the serial loop) when debugging, so
/// per-seed diagnostics print in seed order, or when `BREPPER_SERIAL_COMPETE`
/// is set; otherwise `BREPPER_THREADS` or the machine's parallelism. The result
/// is the same either way — see `compete_region`.
fn competition_threads(debug: bool) -> usize {
    if debug || std::env::var_os("BREPPER_SERIAL_COMPETE").is_some() {
        return 1;
    }
    std::env::var("BREPPER_THREADS")
        .ok()
        .and_then(|v| v.parse::<usize>().ok())
        .filter(|&n| n >= 1)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| std::thread::available_parallelism().map_or(1, |n| n.get()))
}

/// `f(seed)` for every seed in `seeds`, on up to `threads` threads, keyed by
/// seed. Workers share the run's fit memo.
fn evaluate_seeds<T, F>(
    seeds: &[usize],
    threads: usize,
    cache: Option<super::surface::FitCache>,
    f: F,
) -> std::collections::HashMap<usize, T>
where
    T: Send,
    F: Fn(usize) -> T + Sync,
{
    let workers = threads.min(seeds.len());
    if workers <= 1 {
        return seeds.iter().map(|&s| (s, f(s))).collect();
    }
    let next = std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0);
    std::thread::scope(|scope| {
        let handles: Vec<_> = (0..workers)
            .map(|_| {
                let cache = cache.clone();
                let (next, f) = (&next, &f);
                std::thread::Builder::new()
                    // Stage 2's own thread runs on the 8 MB main stack; give
                    // workers the same headroom rather than the 2 MB default.
                    .stack_size(8 << 20)
                    .spawn_scoped(scope, move || {
                        super::surface::with_shared_fit_cache(cache, || {
                            let mut out = Vec::new();
                            loop {
                                let i = next.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
                                let Some(&seed) = seeds.get(i) else { break };
                                out.push((seed, f(seed)));
                            }
                            out
                        })
                    })
                    .expect("spawn competition worker")
            })
            .collect();
        handles
            .into_iter()
            .flat_map(|h| h.join().expect("competition worker panicked"))
            .collect()
    })
}
'''
```

```bash
cat >> tests/integration/stage2_competition.rs <<'EOF'

/// Every selected surface at full precision, in selection order: the
/// fingerprint two stage-2 runs must agree on bit for bit.
fn fingerprint(out: &stage2::Stage2Output) -> Vec<String> {
    out.selected_surfaces
        .iter()
        .map(|s| match s {
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Planar(i) => format!("{:?}", out.planar_hypotheses[*i]),
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Conical(i) => format!("{:?}", out.conical_hypotheses[*i]),
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Spherical(i) => format!("{:?}", out.spherical_hypotheses[*i]),
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Toroidal(i) => format!("{:?}", out.toroidal_hypotheses[*i]),
            stage2::SelectedSurface::BSpline(i) => {
                let b = &out.bspline_hypotheses[*i];
                format!("bspline {:?} {:?} {:?}", b.faces, b.error_max, b.centroid_error_max)
            }
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Competition evaluates seeds speculatively on worker threads and applies
/// the results in seed order, so the thread count must not change a single
/// bit of stage 2's output — and the output must not depend on hash-set
/// iteration order, which differs between `HashSet` instances even within one
/// process. These two models each showed run-to-run differences in their
/// fitted parameters' last bits before 2026-10-16 (a plane offset summed in
/// `HashSet` order; candidate axes collected in it), so a reintroduced
/// order dependence is likely to show up here too.
#[test]
fn competition_is_thread_count_independent() {
    for model in [
        "tests/ccad/generated/cone_cylinder.stl",
        "tests/ccad/generated/filleted_pipe.stl",
    ] {
        let stl = format!("{}/{model}", manifest_dir());
        let run_with = |threads: &str| {
            let config =
                config::parse_config_from(["brepper", &stl, "--stage=2", "-q", threads]).unwrap();
            let mesh = stage1::stage1(&config).expect("stage1 should pass");
            fingerprint(&stage2::stage2(&config, mesh, None).expect("stage2 should pass"))
        };
        let serial = run_with("--threads=1");
        assert!(!serial.is_empty(), "{model}: no surfaces");
        assert_eq!(run_with("--threads=1"), serial, "{model}: two serial runs differ");
        assert_eq!(run_with("--threads=4"), serial, "{model}: 4 threads differ from 1");
    }
}
EOF
```

```bash
dispatcher='''/// The serial seed loop — `for seed in seeds { if !skip { apply(evaluate) } }`
/// — with seeds evaluated ahead of their turn on `threads` workers.
///
/// **Why the result is the serial loop's, bit for bit.** `evaluate` reads only
/// the mesh, the region and the seed — never the claims — so its value for a
/// seed does not depend on when, or on which thread, it is computed. Claims
/// decide only WHETHER a seed is used, and results are applied strictly in seed
/// order with the skip rule re-checked against the claims as they stand at that
/// seed's turn. A seed is dispatched only if unskipped at dispatch, and claims
/// only grow, so a seed skipped at dispatch is skipped at its turn too.
///
/// **Why it wastes little.** A seed evaluated ahead is wasted only if a commit
/// lands while it is in flight and makes it skippable. Measured, those are the
/// expensive ones: a seed inside a large surface regrows that whole surface, so
/// on `rounded_cube_10_r2_fine` speculating in fixed blocks wasted 101 s of
/// evaluation to use 36 s. So the number in flight drops to ONE after every
/// commit and doubles (to `threads`) after every seed that commits nothing: a
/// freeform region, where nothing commits, runs fully parallel; a commit-heavy
/// analytic region runs nearly serially and wastes almost nothing.
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
fn evaluate_seeds_in_order<T, Skip, Eval, Apply>(
    seeds: &[usize],
    threads: usize,
    cache: Option<super::surface::FitCache>,
    skip: Skip,
    evaluate: Eval,
    mut apply: Apply,
    claimed: &mut Vec<bool>,
) where
    T: Send,
    Skip: Fn(usize, &[bool]) -> bool,
    Eval: Fn(usize) -> T + Sync,
    Apply: FnMut(T, &mut Vec<bool>) -> bool,
{
    enum Slot<T> {
        Waiting,
        Skipped,
        InFlight,
        Done(T),
    }
    let n = seeds.len();
    std::thread::scope(|scope| {
        let (job_tx, job_rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<Option<(usize, usize)>>();
        let job_rx = std::sync::Mutex::new(job_rx);
        let (res_tx, res_rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<(usize, T)>();
        for _ in 0..threads {
            let (job_rx, res_tx, cache, evaluate) = (&job_rx, res_tx.clone(), cache.clone(), &evaluate);
            std::thread::Builder::new()
                // Stage 2's own thread runs on the 8 MB main stack; give workers
                // the same headroom rather than the 2 MB default.
                .stack_size(8 << 20)
                .spawn_scoped(scope, move || {
                    super::surface::with_shared_fit_cache(cache, || loop {
                        let job = job_rx.lock().expect("job queue").recv();
                        let Ok(Some((i, seed))) = job else { break };
                        if res_tx.send((i, evaluate(seed))).is_err() {
                            break;
                        }
                    })
                })
                .expect("spawn competition worker");
        }
        drop(res_tx);

        let mut slots: Vec<Slot<T>> = (0..n).map(|_| Slot::Waiting).collect();
        let (mut next_dispatch, mut next_apply, mut in_flight, mut window) = (0, 0, 0, 1);
        while next_apply < n {
            while in_flight < window && next_dispatch < n {
                let seed = seeds[next_dispatch];
                if skip(seed, claimed) {
                    slots[next_dispatch] = Slot::Skipped;
                } else {
                    job_tx.send(Some((next_dispatch, seed))).expect("workers alive");
                    slots[next_dispatch] = Slot::InFlight;
                    in_flight += 1;
                }
                next_dispatch += 1;
            }
            while next_apply < next_dispatch {
                match std::mem::replace(&mut slots[next_apply], Slot::Waiting) {
                    Slot::Skipped => {}
                    Slot::Done(result) => {
                        if !skip(seeds[next_apply], claimed) {
                            window = if apply(result, claimed) { 1 } else { (window * 2).min(threads) };
                        }
                    }
                    other => {
                        slots[next_apply] = other;
                        break;
                    }
                }
                next_apply += 1;
            }
            if next_apply < n && in_flight > 0 && matches!(slots[next_apply], Slot::InFlight) {
                let (i, result) = res_rx.recv().expect("workers alive");
                slots[i] = Slot::Done(result);
                in_flight -= 1;
            }
        }
        for _ in 0..threads {
            let _ = job_tx.send(None);
        }
        // Results for seeds still in flight are not needed; let workers finish.
        while in_flight > 0 {
            let _ = res_rx.recv();
            in_flight -= 1;
        }
    });
}
```

```
) -> (Vec<CompeteHyp>, Vec<usize>) {
    let n = mesh.faces.len();
    let debug = config.verbosity >= 3 || std::env::var("BREPPER_DEBUG_COMPETE").is_ok();
    let mut in_region = vec![false; n];
    for &fi in &region.faces {
        in_region[fi] = true;
    }

    // Region curvature scale: a face reads "flat" when its principal
    // curvature radius exceeds a couple of region diameters.
    let extent = region_extent(mesh, region);
    let flat_eps = if extent > 0.0 { 1.0 / (2.0 * extent) } else { 1e-6 };

    // Seed order: jet-interior-first (ascending curvature mismatch with
    // region neighbors), ties by face index for determinism.
    let mut seeds = region.faces.clone();
    let score: Vec<f64> = (0..n)
        .map(|fi| {
            if !in_region[fi] {
                return f64::INFINITY;
            }
            neighbor_jet_mismatch(mesh, fi, jet, &in_region)
        })
        .collect();
    seeds.sort_by(|&a, &b| {
        score[a]
            .partial_cmp(&score[b])
            .unwrap()
            .then_with(|| a.cmp(&b))
    });

    // Every region face seeds exactly once — \`seeds\` is a permutation of them,
    // which is what terminates the loop. Committing a hypothesis does NOT
    // remove the faces it grew into from the seed pool.
    //
    // Growing into a face is a hypothesis, not a conclusion. The committed
    // face set is always a \`flood\` output, so every member validates — but
    // against a fit whose parameters came from an unvalidated seed
    // neighbourhood, so "validated" does not mean "the right surface". Letting
    // those faces seed too means a wrong hypothesis can be out-competed by a
    // right one grown from a face it had swallowed; \`resolve_claims\` already
    // exists to arbitrate the multi-claims that produces.
    //
    // It also makes the long-standing claim that seed misordering "costs only
    // time" actually true: previously an early bad hypothesis consumed faces a
    // later, better seed needed.
    let mut committed: Vec<CompeteHyp> = Vec::new();
    let mut claim_lists: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); n]; // face -> committed idxs
    let mut claimed = vec![false; n];

    // Skip only faces in the INTERIOR of what is already explained: every
    // neighbour claimed too. Seeding there cannot produce a competitor — a fit
    // grown from the middle of a validated surface refits that same surface —
```

```
pub(super) fn compete_from_seed(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    seed: usize,
    jet: &[JetField],
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &CompeteConfig,
    flat_eps: f64,
    debug: bool,
) -> Option<(CompeteHyp, f64, u8)> {
    {
        let jf = jet[seed];
        // Dominant / secondary principal-curvature MAGNITUDES. The jet orders
        // k1 ≥ k2 by signed value, so for a concave feature (a hole wall,
        // κ = −1/r) the dominant curvature is negative and lands in k2 —
        // taking |k1| as the dominant would read the wall's flat axial
        // direction and treat the hole as planar. Order by magnitude instead.
        let a1 = jf.k1.abs().max(jf.k2.abs());
        let a2 = jf.k1.abs().min(jf.k2.abs());

        // Grow the jet-pruned candidate types; keep the largest validated
        // area (simplest-DOF tiebreak).
        let mut best: Option<(CompeteHyp, f64, u8)> = None; // (hyp, area, dof)
        let consider = |hyp_area: Option<(CompeteHyp, f64)>, dof: u8, best: &mut Option<(CompeteHyp, f64, u8)>| {
            if let Some((h, area)) = hyp_area {
                let sweep = candidate_sweep(mesh, &h);
                if sweep < MIN_AXIAL_SWEEP_DEG.to_radians() {
                    if debug {
                        eprintln!(
                            "    compete: seed {seed} rejected {} sweeping only {:.1}\u{00b0} about its axis — radius undetermined ({} faces, area {area:.2})",
                            h.kind_name(),
                            sweep.to_degrees(),
                            h.faces().len(),
                        );
                    }
                    return;
                }
                let better = match best {
                    None => true,
                    Some((_, ba, bd)) => area > *ba + 1e-9 || ((area - *ba).abs() <= 1e-9 && dof < *bd),
                };
                if better {
                    *best = Some((h, area, dof));
                }
            }
        };

        // Plane is always a candidate (cheap; catches misread flats).
        let plane = grow::<PlanarSurface>(mesh, in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, 1);
        let mut cone_area = None;
        let mut sphere_area = None;
        let mut torus_area = None;
        if a1 >= flat_eps {
            // Curved: a developable (cylinder/cone) is always plausible.
            let cone = grow::<ConicalSurface>(mesh, in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, MIN_CYLINDER_FACES);
            cone_area = cone.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));

            // Toroidal candidate: a direct grow from this seed (fillet tori,
            // bend tubes), skipped when the seed reads sphere-like — every
            // adjacent quad-row band of a sphere lies near some torus, so a
            // (κ,κ) seed's torus is at best a bogus band that loses to the
            // sphere anyway. A torus seed reads |κ2| < |κ1| (κ2 varies
            // azimuthally around the tube; it only approaches κ1 near the
            // degenerate R≈r hole of a donut — a whole-region ladder case,
            // not a competition case).
            let mut torus = if a2 < 0.8 * a1 {
                let patch = seed_patch(mesh, in_region, seed, jet);
                torus_candidate(mesh, in_region, &patch, &[seed], centroids, config)
            } else {
                None
            };
            // Bent-tube promotion: a cylinder that stalled against
            // tube-continuation faces is the developable prefix of a bent
            // tube; grow a torus from the pure-bend patch past the stall.
            if let Some((cyl, _, cyl_faces)) = cone.as_ref() {
                if cyl.is_cylinder() {
                    let promoted =
                        promote_bend(mesh, in_region, cyl, cyl_faces, jet, centroids, config);
                    if let Some(p) = promoted {
                        if torus.as_ref().is_none_or(|(_, a, _)| p.1 > *a) {
                            torus = Some(p);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            torus_area = torus.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));

            consider(cone.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Conical(h), a)), 2, &mut best);
            // Curved in both directions → also try a sphere.
            if a2 >= 0.3 * a1 {
                let sphere = grow::<SphericalSurface>(mesh, in_region, seed, jet, centroids, config, MIN_SPHERE_FACES);
                sphere_area = sphere.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));
                consider(sphere.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Spherical(h), a)), 1, &mut best);
            }
            consider(torus.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Toroidal(h), a)), 3, &mut best);
        }
        let plane_area = plane.as_ref().map(|(_, a, f)| (*a, f.len()));
        consider(plane.map(|(h, a, _)| (CompeteHyp::Planar(h), a)), 0, &mut best);

        if debug && best.is_none() {
            eprintln!(
                "    compete: seed {seed} jet=({:.3},{:.3}) class {:?} → NO GROWTH (plane {plane_area:?} cone {cone_area:?} sphere {sphere_area:?} torus {torus_area:?})",
                jf.k1, jf.k2, curvature_class(jf),
            );
        }

        if let Some((hyp, area, dof)) = best.as_ref() {
            if debug {
                eprintln!(
                    "    compete: seed {seed} → {} ({} faces, area {area:.2}, dof {dof}, sweep {:.1}\u{00b0})",
                    hyp.kind_name(),
                    hyp.faces().len(),
                    match hyp {
                        CompeteHyp::Toroidal(t) => torus_sweep(mesh, t).to_degrees(),
                        CompeteHyp::Conical(c) => conical_sweep(mesh, c).to_degrees(),
                        _ => 0.0,
                    }
                );
            }
        }
        best
    }
}

/// Resolve multi-claimed faces to their best-fitting claimant (2× margin to
/// leave the larger claimant), rebuild each hypothesis's face/vertex lists,
/// drop hypotheses that lost all faces, and collect unclaimed leftovers.
/// Is every neighbour of \`fi\` claimed too? Such a face is interior to the
/// explained set and cannot seed anything new.
```

```
pub(super) fn grow_from<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    in_region: &[bool],
    start: usize,
    initial: Vec<usize>,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &CompeteConfig,
    min_faces: usize,
) -> Option<(S::Hypothesis, f64, Vec<usize>)> {
    let stol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
    let vtol = config.vertex_tolerance_mm;
    let mut accepted =
        condition_patch::<S>(mesh, start, initial, centroids, config, vtol, stol, min_faces);
    // The last fit and the flood it produced, keyed by the exact face list it
    // was fitted on. Fitting and flooding are deterministic functions of that
    // list, so whenever the loop comes back to it — a flood that reproduces its
    // own input, which is how this loop usually converges, and then the final
    // fit below — the stored pair IS what recomputing would return. Reusing it
    // changes no result and skips the most expensive call in stage 2 (a torus
    // or cone LM) about once per grow.
    let mut last: Option<(Vec<usize>, S::Fit, Vec<usize>)> = None;
    let mut fit_and_flood = |faces: &Vec<usize>| -> Option<(S::Fit, Vec<usize>)> {
        if let Some((key, fit, comp)) = &last {
            if key == faces {
                return Some((fit.clone(), comp.clone()));
            }
        }
        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, faces);
        let mut fit = super::surface::cached_fit::<S>(mesh, faces, &verts, config.verbosity)?;
        S::determine_convexity(mesh, faces, &mut fit);
        let comp = flood::<S>(mesh, in_region, start, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol);
        last = Some((faces.clone(), fit.clone(), comp.clone()));
        Some((fit, comp))
    };
    let mut prev = 0usize;
    for round in 0..MAX_GROW_ROUNDS {
        let (_, comp) = fit_and_flood(&accepted)?;
        if comp.is_empty() {
            return None; // the start face does not lie on its own fit — reject
        }
        if comp.len() == accepted.len() && round > 0 {
            accepted = comp;
            break;
        }
        if comp.len() == prev {
            // Oscillating between two sizes — stop at the larger.
            if comp.len() >= accepted.len() {
                accepted = comp;
            }
            break;
        }
        prev = accepted.len();
        accepted = comp;
    }

    // Final fit + validated flood.
    let (fit, faces) = fit_and_flood(&accepted)?;
    if faces.len() < min_faces {
        return None;
    }
    let area: f64 = faces.iter().map(|&fi| face_area(&mesh.faces[fi], &mesh.vertices)).sum();
    let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &faces);
    let hyp = S::make_hypothesis(mesh, faces.clone(), verts, &fit);
    Some((hyp, area, faces))
}


/// A committed torus's minor radius may not exceed this fraction of its major
/// radius. Real fillets and bend tubes are slim (r/R ≤ 0.5 across the corpus:
/// full donut 0.3, pipe-elbow 0.5, fillets 0.15–0.2); an r ≈ R "fat" torus is
/// a bogus fit a flat cap or wall band accepts loosely and then wins on area
/// (filleted_pipe: an r/R = 0.82 torus ate an annular end cap).
const MAX_TORUS_RADIUS_RATIO: f64 = 0.7;

/// How far a support sweeps around an axis, in radians: the angular extent of
/// \`verts\` about the line through \`origin\` along \`axis\`, taken as 2π minus the
/// largest angular gap between consecutive vertices, so a patch straddling the
/// angle origin measures correctly.
///
/// This is the observable that says whether a rotational parameter is
/// determined by the data at all. A surface of revolution fitted to a patch
/// that never goes around its axis has its radius free, and a free parameter is
/// worse than useless in competition: the fit becomes a super-model of the
/// simpler surface it should have lost to — covering everything that surface
/// covers, then flooding a little further on the slack — so it takes the
/// largest-validated-area contest every time. See \`MIN_TORUS_SWEEP_DEG\` and
/// \`MIN_CYLINDER_SWEEP_DEG\`.
fn axial_sweep(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    verts: &[usize],
    origin: &[f64; 3],
    axis: &[f64; 3],
) -> f64 {
    let (u, w) = super::perpendicular_basis(axis);
    let mut angles: Vec<f64> = verts
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|&vi| {
            let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
            let d = [v.x - origin[0], v.y - origin[1], v.z - origin[2]];
            let (x, y) = (
                d[0] * u[0] + d[1] * u[1] + d[2] * u[2],
                d[0] * w[0] + d[1] * w[1] + d[2] * w[2],
            );
            // A vertex on the axis has no meaningful angle.
            (x.hypot(y) > 1e-12).then(|| y.atan2(x))
        })
        .collect();
    if angles.len() < 2 {
        return 0.0;
    }
    angles.sort_by(|p, q| p.partial_cmp(q).unwrap());
    let mut gap = angles[0] + std::f64::consts::TAU - angles[angles.len() - 1];
    for pair in angles.windows(2) {
        gap = gap.max(pair[1] - pair[0]);
    }
    (std::f64::consts::TAU - gap).max(0.0)
}

/// Sweep of a candidate's support about the axis whose radius it determines.
/// Planes and spheres have no axis — a sphere's radius is pinned by any patch —
/// so they report a full turn and are never rejected on this ground.
pub(super) fn candidate_sweep(mesh: &ConnectedMesh, hyp: &CompeteHyp) -> f64 {
    match hyp {
        CompeteHyp::Toroidal(h) => torus_sweep(mesh, h),
        CompeteHyp::Conical(h) => conical_sweep(mesh, h),
        CompeteHyp::Planar(_) | CompeteHyp::Spherical(_) => std::f64::consts::TAU,
    }
fn condition_patch<S: SurfaceType>(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    seed: usize,
    mut patch: Vec<usize>,
    centroids: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &CompeteConfig,
    vtol: f64,
    stol: f64,
    min_faces: usize,
) -> Vec<usize> {
    let floor = min_faces.max(MIN_CONDITION_FACES);
    for _ in 0..PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS {
        if patch.len() <= floor {
            break;
        }
        let verts = vertices_of(mesh, &patch);
        let mut fit = match super::surface::cached_fit::<S>(mesh, &patch, &verts, config.verbosity) {
            Some(f) => f,
            None => {
                // No fit to rank by — shrink toward the seed instead.
                let far = patch
                    .iter()
                    .copied()
                    .filter(|&f| f != seed)
                    .max_by(|&a, &b| {
                        centroid_gap(centroids, seed, a)
                            .partial_cmp(&centroid_gap(centroids, seed, b))
                            .unwrap()
                    });
                match far {
                    Some(f) => {
                        patch.retain(|&p| p != f);
                        continue;
                    }
                    None => break,
                }
            }
        };
        S::determine_convexity(mesh, &patch, &mut fit);
        if face_validates::<S>(mesh, seed, &fit, centroids, vtol, stol) {
            break;
        }
        let worst = patch
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|&f| f != seed)
            .max_by(|&a, &b| {
                face_max_vertex_dist::<S>(mesh, a, &fit)
                    .partial_cmp(&face_max_vertex_dist::<S>(mesh, b, &fit))
                    .unwrap()
            });
        match worst {
            Some(w) => patch.retain(|&f| f != w),
            None => break,
        }
    }
    patch
}
```
</details>

```
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Run-scoped fit memoization
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Cache key: the surface type and its exact fit inputs.
type FitKey = (std::any::TypeId, Vec<usize>, Vec<usize>);
type FitMap = std::collections::HashMap<FitKey, Box<dyn std::any::Any + Send>>;

/// One stage-2 run's fit memo, shared by every thread working on that run.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(super) struct FitCache(std::sync::Arc<std::sync::Mutex<FitMap>>);

thread_local! {
    /// The memo this thread fills and reads, while one is installed.
    static FIT_CACHE: std::cell::RefCell<Option<FitCache>> = const { std::cell::RefCell::new(None) };
}

/// Install \`cache\` on this thread for the duration of \`f\` (also on panic).
fn with_installed<R>(cache: Option<FitCache>, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R {
    struct Restore(Option<FitCache>);
    impl Drop for Restore {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let prev = self.0.take();
            FIT_CACHE.with(|c| *c.borrow_mut() = prev);
        }
    }
    let prev = FIT_CACHE.with(|c| c.replace(cache));
    let _restore = Restore(prev);
    f()
}

/// Run \`f\` with a fresh fit memo installed on this thread (if \`enabled\`), and
/// drop it afterwards.
///
/// **Why it is safe:** \`fit_surface\` is a deterministic function of the mesh,
/// the face list and the vertex list (verbosity only gates printing), and the
/// mesh is borrowed immutably for the whole of stage 2.3–2.4. So a stored fit
/// for an identical \`(type, faces, vertices)\` key is exactly what recomputing
/// would return — every result is bit-identical, whichever thread computed it.
/// The memo is scoped to one stage-2 run so face indices from different meshes
/// can never collide.
///
/// **Why it pays:** competition reaches the same patch from different seeds and
/// flood starts. Measured with a probe, repeated torus fits were 33 s of
/// \`rounded_cube_10_r2_fine\`'s 68 s of torus fitting and 30 s of
/// \`pipe_elbow_10_fine\`'s 124 s.
pub(super) fn with_fit_cache<R>(enabled: bool, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R {
    let cache = enabled.then(|| FitCache(Default::default()));
    with_installed(cache, f)
}

/// The memo installed on this thread, to hand to worker threads.
pub(super) fn current_fit_cache() -> Option<FitCache> {
    FIT_CACHE.with(|c| c.borrow().clone())
}

/// Run \`f\` on a worker thread with the run's memo (from [\`current_fit_cache\`]).
pub(super) fn with_shared_fit_cache<R>(cache: Option<FitCache>, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R {
    with_installed(cache, f)
}

/// \`S::CACHE_FITS\` is set; otherwise a plain call.
```

```bash
    /// Raised when the work this thread is doing has been abandoned; see
    /// [`abandonable`].
    static ABANDONED: std::cell::RefCell<Option<std::sync::Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool>>> =
        const { std::cell::RefCell::new(None) };
}

/// Run `f` with `flag` as its abandon signal: once `flag` is raised, every
/// [`cached_fit`] on this thread returns `None` without fitting, so `f` winds
/// down at its next fit. What `f` then returns is meaningless, and the caller
/// must discard it — competition raises the flag only for a seed evaluated
/// ahead of its turn that the serial loop would skip (see
/// `compete::evaluate_seeds_in_order`).
pub(super) fn abandonable<R>(flag: std::sync::Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool>, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R {
    struct Clear;
    impl Drop for Clear {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            ABANDONED.with(|a| *a.borrow_mut() = None);
        }
    }
    ABANDONED.with(|a| *a.borrow_mut() = Some(flag));
    let _clear = Clear;
    f()
}

fn abandoned() -> bool {
    ABANDONED.with(|a| a.borrow().as_ref().is_some_and(|f| f.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed)))
}
```

```bash
# Dispatcher: bound pending (running + finished-unapplied) seeds; policy knob.
p='src/stage2/compete.rs'
s=open(p).read()
a=s.index('        let mut slots: Vec<Slot<T>> = (0..n).map(|_| Slot::Waiting).collect();')
b=s.index('        for _ in 0..threads {\n            let _ = job_tx.send(None);')
new='''        let mut slots: Vec<Slot<T>> = (0..n).map(|_| Slot::Waiting).collect();
        let (max_window, adaptive, waste_driven) = window_policy(threads);
        // `pending`: seeds dispatched and not yet applied or discarded —
        // running or finished. Bounding it (not just the running count) bounds
        // how far ahead of the serial loop's turn the workers can get.
        let (mut next_dispatch, mut next_apply, mut in_flight, mut pending) = (0, 0, 0, 0);
        let mut window = if adaptive { 1 } else { max_window };
        while next_apply < n {
            while pending < window && next_dispatch < n {
                let seed = seeds[next_dispatch];
                if skip(seed, claimed) {
                    slots[next_dispatch] = Slot::Skipped;
                } else {
                    let abandon = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
                    job_tx.send(Some((next_dispatch, seed, abandon.clone()))).expect("workers alive");
                    slots[next_dispatch] = Slot::InFlight(abandon);
                    in_flight += 1;
                    pending += 1;
                }
                next_dispatch += 1;
            }
            while next_apply < next_dispatch {
                match std::mem::replace(&mut slots[next_apply], Slot::Waiting) {
                    Slot::Skipped => {}
                    Slot::Done(result) => {
                        pending -= 1;
                        if skip(seeds[next_apply], claimed) {
                            if waste_driven {
                                window = (window / 2).max(1);
                            }
                        } else {
                            if waste_driven {
                                window = (window + 1).min(max_window);
                            }
                            let committed = apply(result, claimed);
                            if committed {
                                // Seeds in flight that this commit made skippable
                                // will be discarded at their turn: stop them.
                                for j in next_apply + 1..next_dispatch {
                                    if let Slot::InFlight(abandon) = &slots[j] {
                                        if skip(seeds[j], claimed) {
                                            abandon.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
                                        }
                                    }
                                }
                            }
                            if adaptive {
                                window = if committed { 1 } else { (window * 2).min(max_window) };
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    other => {
                        slots[next_apply] = other;
                        break;
                    }
                }
                next_apply += 1;
            }
            if next_apply < n && in_flight > 0 && matches!(slots[next_apply], Slot::InFlight(_)) {
                let (i, result) = res_rx.recv().expect("workers alive");
                slots[i] = Slot::Done(result);
                in_flight -= 1;
            }
        }
'''
```

```bash
fn evaluate_seeds_in_order<T, Skip, Eval, Apply>(
    seeds: &[usize],
    threads: usize,
    cache: Option<super::surface::FitCache>,
    skip: Skip,
    evaluate: Eval,
    mut apply: Apply,

    Eval: Fn(usize) -> T + Sync,
    Apply: FnMut(T, &mut Vec<bool>),
{
    enum Slot<T> {
        Waiting,
        Skipped,
        Running,
        Done(T),
    }
    type Outcome<T> = std::thread::Result<T>;
    let n = seeds.len();
    let (job_tx, job_rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<(usize, usize)>();
    let job_rx = std::sync::Mutex::new(job_rx);
    let (res_tx, res_rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<(usize, Outcome<T>)>();
    std::thread::scope(|scope| {
        // Owned here so that it drops — and the workers exit — however this
        // closure ends, including by a panic.
        let job_tx = job_tx;

            let (job_rx, res_tx, cache, evaluate) = (&job_rx, res_tx.clone(), cache.clone(), &evaluate);

                // the same headroom rather than the 2 MB default.
                .stack_size(8 << 20)
                .spawn_scoped(scope, move || {

                        let job = job_rx.lock().expect("job queue").recv();
                        let Ok((i, seed)) = job else { break };
                        // A panic goes back to the dispatcher, which re-raises
                        // it; left here it would leave the dispatcher waiting.
                        let outcome = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| evaluate(seed)));
                        if res_tx.send((i, outcome)).is_err() {
                            break;
                        }
                    })
                })
                .expect("spawn competition worker");
        }
        drop(res_tx);

        let mut slots: Vec<Slot<T>> = (0..n).map(|_| Slot::Waiting).collect();
        // `pending` counts seeds dispatched and not yet applied, running or done.
        let (mut next_dispatch, mut next_apply, mut pending, mut window) = (0, 0, 0, threads);
        while next_apply < n {
            while pending < window && next_dispatch < n {
                let seed = seeds[next_dispatch];
                slots[next_dispatch] = if skip(seed, claimed) {
                    Slot::Skipped
                } else {
                    job_tx.send((next_dispatch, seed)).expect("workers alive");
                    pending += 1;
                    Slot::Running
                };
                next_dispatch += 1;
            }
            while next_apply < next_dispatch {
                match std::mem::replace(&mut slots[next_apply], Slot::Waiting) {
                    Slot::Skipped => {}
                    Slot::Done(result) => {
                        pending -= 1;
                        if skip(seeds[next_apply], claimed) {
                            window = (window / 2).max(1);
                        } else {
                            window = (window + 1).min(threads);
                            apply(result, claimed);
                        }
                    }
                    running => {
                        slots[next_apply] = running;
                        break;
                    }
                }
                next_apply += 1;
            }
            // Stopped short of `next_dispatch`: the seed whose turn it is is
            // still running, so wait for a result.
            if next_apply < next_dispatch {
                let (i, outcome) = res_rx.recv().expect("workers alive");
                match outcome {
                    Ok(result) => slots[i] = Slot::Done(result),
                    Err(panic) => std::panic::resume_unwind(panic),
                }
            }
        }
    });
```

```
//! seed floods — vertex tolerance the arbiter — to its entire true extent,
//! and largest-validated-area then selects it over the accidental one.
//!
//! Faces no hypothesis claims are returned as leftovers; the caller degrades
//! them to per-facet planes (freeform fitting is stage 2.3(e), a later step).

use std::collections::HashSet;

use crate::config::Config;
use crate::stage1::ConnectedMesh;

use super::surface::SurfaceType;
use super::conical::{ConeFit, ConicalSurface};
use super::edges::JetField;
use super::planar::PlanarSurface;
use super::regions::Region;
use super::spherical::{bounding_box_diagonal, SphericalSurface};
use super::toroidal::ToroidalSurface;

use super::{
    face_area, ConicalHypothesis, PlanarHypothesis, SphericalHypothesis, ToroidalHypothesis,
    MIN_CYLINDER_FACES, MIN_SPHERE_FACES, MIN_TORUS_FACES,
};

/// The three settings competition reads, as a plain \`Sync\` value.
///
/// \`Config\` carries the \`--compare\` reference shape, an OCCT handle, so it
/// cannot be shared across threads — and competition, which \`compete_region\`
/// runs on several, never reads it. The field names match \`Config\`'s so the code
/// below reads exactly as it did when it took \`&Config\`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct CompeteConfig {
    pub vertex_tolerance_mm: f64,
    pub surface_tolerance_mm: f64,
    pub verbosity: u8,
    /// \`--threads\`; \`None\` = all cores.
    pub threads: Option<usize>,
}

impl From<&Config> for CompeteConfig {
    fn from(c: &Config) -> Self {
        CompeteConfig {
            vertex_tolerance_mm: c.vertex_tolerance_mm,
            surface_tolerance_mm: c.surface_tolerance_mm,
            verbosity: c.verbosity,
            threads: c.threads,
        }
    }
}

/// Max faces in the jet-similar seed patch used to condition the initial fit.
const SEED_PATCH_CAP: usize = 32;

/// Max trim rounds when conditioning a seed patch (one worst face per round).
const PATCH_TRIM_ROUNDS: usize = 16;
```

```
+    pub threads: Option<usize>,

+impl From<&Config> for CompeteConfig {

+fn competition_threads(debug: bool, requested: Option<usize>) -> usize {
+    if debug {
+        return 1;
+    }
+    requested
+        .filter(|&n| n >= 1)
+        .unwrap_or_else(|| std::thread::available_parallelism().map_or(1, |n| n.get()))

+/// The serial seed loop — \`for seed in seeds { if !skip(seed) { apply(evaluate(seed)) } }\`
+/// — with seeds evaluated ahead of their turn on \`threads\` workers.
+///
+/// **Why the result is the serial loop's, bit for bit.** \`evaluate\` reads only
+/// the mesh, the region and the seed — never the claims — so its value for a
+/// seed does not depend on when, or on which thread, it is computed. Claims
+/// decide only WHETHER a seed is used, and results are applied strictly in seed
+/// order with the skip rule re-checked against the claims as they stand at that
+/// seed's turn. A seed is dispatched only if unskipped at dispatch, and claims
+/// only grow, so a seed skipped at dispatch is skipped at its turn too.
+///
```

```
+/// Every selected surface at full precision, in selection order: the

+
+/// Competition evaluates seeds speculatively on worker threads and applies
+/// the results in seed order, so the thread count must not change a single
+/// bit of stage 2's output — and the output must not depend on hash-set
+/// iteration order, which differs between \`HashSet\` instances even within one
+/// process. This model showed run-to-run differences in its
+/// fitted parameters' last bits before 2026-10-16 (a plane offset summed in
+/// \`HashSet\` order; candidate axes collected in it), so a reintroduced
+/// order dependence is likely to show up here too.
+#[test]
+fn competition_is_thread_count_independent() {
+    // One small model: it exhibited the run-to-run difference, and the test
+    // must stay cheap — it runs stage 2 three times.
+    let model = "tests/ccad/generated/cone_cylinder.stl";
+    let stl = format!("{}/{model}", manifest_dir());
+    let run_with = |threads: &str| {
+        let config =
+            config::parse_config_from(["brepper", &stl, "--stage=2", "-q", threads]).unwrap();
+        let mesh = stage1::stage1(&config).expect("stage1 should pass");
+        fingerprint(&stage2::stage2(&config, mesh, None).expect("stage2 should pass"))
+    };
+    let serial = run_with("--threads=1");
+    assert!(!serial.is_empty(), "{model}: no surfaces");
+    assert_eq!(run_with("--threads=1"), serial, "{model}: two serial runs differ");
```

```bash
version matched on 159 of 159 corpus models that complete.

commit makes it skippable, and those are the expensive seeds (one inside a
large surface regrows it). With ten seeds always in hand rounded_cube fine
wasted 71 of 128 evaluations (130 s CPU for a 31.6 s serial job). The window
```

## 🤖 Assistant
<!-- msg_011Cg6X4Etrv2pZJqiabwSU8 -->

The test suite now runs in **3:05** (down from 4:32) and is green: 493 passed, 0 failed, 32 ignored. It's committed as `55fe0c4`.

**What changed.** Instead of changing what stage 2.3 competition decides, as in the option you picked, I changed where it runs. The output is identical, so no corpus sweep was needed. The step that scores each seed face never looks at what earlier seeds claimed, so worker threads can score seeds ahead of their turn. The results are still applied one at a time in seed order, exactly as the serial loop would.

**Results are bit-identical.** At full precision, 1 thread and 10 threads give the same output on six models. A new test, `competition_is_thread_count_independent`, checks this.

**How far ahead to work was the real problem.** A seed scored early is wasted if an earlier seed claims its surface first, and those tend to be the expensive seeds. Always scoring 10 seeds ahead burned 130 s of CPU on `rounded_cube_10_r2_fine`, which takes 31.6 s serially. Now the number of seeds worked on ahead halves each time one is wasted and grows by one each time one is used, up to two per thread. Stage 2 with ten threads (wall / CPU, against serial wall):

| model | serial | parallel |
|---|---|---|
| `rounded_cube_10_r2_fine` | 31.6 s | 20.7 s / 58 s |
| `pipe_elbow_10_fine` | 101 s | 16.5 s / 129 s |
| `bspline_hill` (freeform) | 215 s | 30.6 s / 279 s |

I tried three other ways to limit the waste and dropped them. Their measurements are in `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md` under "Suite runtime".

**Two bugs found along the way.** Stage 2 wasn't deterministic before this: the same binary gave slightly different fitted values from run to run on 5 of 7 models. Two spots summed or collected values in `HashSet` order, which changes per run: the plane fit and the step that collects candidate axes from neighbouring surfaces. Both now go through the values in sorted order, and the new test failed 3 times out of 3 without these fixes.

**Also in the commit:** a `--threads=<N>` option (added to the README), and debug runs at `-v 3` or higher stay single-threaded so their output prints in seed order.

The suite now keeps all 10 cores busy for its whole run, so further cuts have to come from doing less work rather than spreading it out. I've put up a card for a session that would profile where the CPU goes and look for speed-ups that keep output bit-identical.

```
### The measured starting point

whose six vertices lie in two rings of three spanning 31.3° of arc:

----
### Option C — two circles from the ring structure

Two ruling-aligned quads give six vertices in two rings of three, one per rim.
Three points in space determine a unique circle, so each rim yields a centre, a
radius and a normal; the line through the two centres is the axis and the two
radii at two heights give the half-angle by similar triangles. Exact, vertices
only, non-iterative, and it works from **2 facets**.

Measured on the seed above: axis **0.0002°** off, half-angle **0.0001°** off,
the two radii recovered to 0.1–0.2× vtol, against a mesh error of 4.1e-7 mm.
Conditioning is comfortable rather than marginal — the rings span 31.3°, and the
sensitivity \`2ε/α²\` gives a radius uncertainty of 1.1e-5 mm, under a quarter of
vtol.

**Cost and weakness.** Needs the ruling structure the other options do not: two
rings with ≥3 points each, i.e. ruling-aligned facets. Phase 1.0 measured 25.6%
of corpus cylinder facets straddling three or more rulings, so this cannot be the
only route. Ring identification needs no provisional axis — the shared edge
between two quads in a strip *is* a ruling, so its endpoints are one per ring and
walking the strip labels the rest combinatorially.

**Built 2026-10-15 as \`initialize::cone_from_rings\`; measured; not wired.** Two
departures from the design above, and the reason it stays unwired.

- *Rims are found, not labelled.* "A shared edge is a ruling" holds only for
  quads in one band; in a triangle strip the shared edges alternate between
  rulings and diagonals. Instead every split of the seed's vertices into two
  groups of ≥3 is tried — at most \`2^(n−1)\`, with \`n\` capped at 10 by a work
  bound that decides nothing — each scored by the largest distance of any vertex
  from the cone the split implies. The true split scores at the mesh's own
  precision and a wrong one misses by a wide margin. Unit-tested exact to 1e-9 at
  10°–84°, from **two quads or four triangles** alike.
- *Taper, not apex.* The profile is \`ρ = r₁ + t·h\`, so a split reading \`t = 0\`
  is a cylinder at a regular point rather than an apex at infinity (and is left
  to the caller's own cylinder route).

**Why it is not wired: two coaxial circles always lie on a cone.** A single band
of *any* surface of revolution has its vertices on two coaxial circles, so this
route finds an **exact** cone on a band of a torus fillet just as it does on a
real cone. Wired into \`fit_surface\` it committed a 17-face, 360° impostor cone on
\`filleted_pipe\` and broke that model. Nothing at band level separates the two —
not the residual, and not the facet normals either, because a facet's plane is
fixed by vertices that lie on both surfaces. This is the Invariants section's
"two circles lie exactly on a sphere" with the sphere replaced by a cone, and it
belongs to the same family of answers: discrimination has to come from beyond
the band (the torus continues smoothly into the next band; the cone's band ends
at its rims), i.e. from competition or branching, not from a better fit.

### Considered and rejected

- **Solving the 6-DOF system from exactly six points.** Exactly determined, so
  finitely many right circular cones pass through them — but a polynomial system
  with multiple roots and no least-squares character. It is also the configuration
  where a *second exact cone* was measured: on one \`simple_cone\` seed the fitter
  returned half-angle 72.85° with its apex 10.8 patch-extents away, explaining the
  six vertices to 6.7e-16 mm, i.e. better than the true cone manages against a
  float32 mesh. Six points genuinely admit more than one cone; Option C escapes
  that only because the ring structure supplies information beyond the six
  positions.
- **Reordering \`compute_truncated_cone_axis\` to try the exact normal-difference
  method before the apex→centroid guess.** Tried, and much worse — see the DO-NOT
  note on that function. Differencing near-identical normals destroys the signal.
- **Orthogonal-distance geometric fitting** (Lukács et al.; Ahn, *Least Squares
  Orthogonal Distance Fitting of Curves and Surfaces*, Springer LNCS 3151). This
  is the right *refinement* and is essentially what the existing LM already does.
  It does not address initialization, which is where every measured failure is.

### Sources

- Andrews, J.; Séquin, C. H. *Type-Constrained Direct Fitting of Quadric
  Surfaces.* Computer-Aided Design & Applications 10(a), 2013.
- Andrews, J.; Séquin, C. H. *Generalized, basis-independent kinematic surface
  fitting.* Computer-Aided Design 45, 2013, 615–620.
```

```
I'm noticing the cone with 17 faces and a 360° sweep on filleted_pipe likely represents a facet band around a torus fillet junction, with all vertices lying on two circular rings.

Since any two coaxial circles lie exactly on some cone, this is a known identifiability problem — a single band of a surface of revolution (torus, sphere) will always be fit exactly by a cone through its two rim circles, even when the true surface isn't a cone. But the rings-based route is capped at ≤10 vertex supports, so a 17-face, ~34-vertex band can't be produced directly from that route alone — it must emerge from a small seed patch whose exact cone fit then validates and grows across the full band.

=========
 single band of points genuinely can't distinguish a cone from a torus, since both fit equally well with just six vertices, meaning the two-rim route is operating squarely in a non-identifiable regime that no amount of local gating can fix.

On a real cone, the band spans the whole surface, so fitting a cone through two rims gives the true cone exactly — but on a torus, that same cone fit is just as exact, making it an impostor. The only real way to discriminate is structural: looking at whether the surface extends beyond the band into more area, which is what the identifiability guards and largest-validated-area principle are supposed to capture, though I need to check why the torus fit in filleted_pipe failed to beat the cone's face count.

So the cone (17 faces) is just one band, while a torus hypothesis would try to cover all bands — meaning area should favor the torus if that fit succeeds. The cone only wins at a given seed when the torus fit grows poorly or fails, so the right approach is to run all hypotheses per seed and commit to whichever one validates the largest area.

Given the regression risk, the pragmatic path is to keep \`cone_from_rings\` as a built, unit-tested initializer without wiring it into fit_surface's gated block — matching how other Phase 1.1 initializers are currently handled, since wiring it in causes regressions. ## 🤖 Assistant
```
<!-- msg_011Cg6XMDSWzemJCgdQsQQnJ -->

Yes, the program finds the much larger rounded edge, but the larger size doesn't protect it. I turned Option C back on in a scratch build to check this; the code in the repo is unchanged.

## The paragraph in plain terms

The program reads a mesh (a surface made of many small flat facets) and works out which simple shapes the original design was built from: flat faces, cylinders, cones, balls, and rounded edges. A rounded edge, or fillet, is a slice of a donut shape (a torus). The program starts from a few facets and asks "what shape is this?", then grows that guess outward.

On a cone, a guess built from only two facets often failed. Option C is an exact shortcut for that case. Two neighbouring facets on a cone have their corners on two circles, a top rim and a bottom rim, and those two circles define the cone exactly.

The catch is that you can always fit a lampshade through two stacked circles. Every round surface (cylinder, ball, rounded edge) gets meshed in rings of facets whose corners lie on two circles. So Option C "finds" a perfect cone on one ring of a rounded edge just as confidently as on a real cone. Looking only at that ring, nothing tells them apart: the corners are where they are, and both shapes pass through them exactly.

## Why the false cone wins

The test model `filleted_pipe` is a tube with rounded edges. The false cone is a ring of 17 facets (4.5 mm²) right where the outer wall meets the top rounded edge. The real rounded edge is found too: all 432 facets (140 mm²), including those 17. That's 30 times the area, yet the cone keeps the ring, for two reasons:

- **"Biggest area wins" only compares guesses grown from the same starting facet.** The false cone grew from a starting facet where the rounded-edge attempt found nothing at all. With Option C off, that facet produces no surface and is harmlessly ignored. With it on, the cone is the only candidate there, so it's accepted. The full rounded edge is only found later, from other facets.
- **When two accepted shapes overlap, a shared facet goes to the simpler shape**, as long as both fit it. The order is flat, ball, cone, torus. That rule exists for good reason: a facet right on the seam between a wall and its rounded edge fits both, and it should belong to the wall. Here, though, it hands the whole 17-facet ring to the cone and cuts it out of the rounded edge.

## What goes wrong in the output

- **The structure is wrong.** The model has 9 faces instead of 8: a thin cone strip that doesn't exist in the design. Also, the seam between the wall and the rounded edge sits 0.29 mm from where it should be, with extra corner points. Anyone editing the model in CAD would hit a phantom face, and re-sizing the fillet or measuring along that seam would go wrong.
- **The shape barely changes.** The cone hugs the rounded edge, so the surface moves by only a few microns. That's my estimate; I didn't measure it.
- **It fails silently.** The tests catch it only because they compare against the original design (0.29 mm off, against a 0.00005 mm tolerance). Without a reference model, which is normal use, the program exits successfully and writes the wrong model. A clean failure would be better.

This isn't specific to this model: any rounded edge could lose a ring this way.

## What leaving Option C off costs

The wide-cone fix alone takes the three cone test models from 4/7/10 to 8/12/12 working starting points out of 12. All three still come out correct, because other starting points on the same cone succeed. The 4 missing ones on `simple_cone` are lost safety margin. They would matter most on small or coarsely meshed cones, where there are few starting points to fall back on.

Making Option C safe needs evidence from beyond the ring. A real cone stops at its rims, while a rounded edge keeps curving into the next ring. One simple version: if a shape lies entirely inside a larger shape that also fits all of its facets, throw it out. That would remove this false cone without breaking the wall-versus-rounded-edge rule, since a wall is never inside its fillet. It's untested, so I've put up a card for a session that would try it and check the whole test collection for regressions.

```
+/// Committed hypotheses that are redundant: every one of their faces is also
+/// claimed, and explained within \`vtol\`, by a single other claimant of strictly
+/// larger area. Returns \`(dropped, container)\` per hypothesis.
+///
+/// Per-face resolution alone cannot see this. It hands a face several claimants
+/// explain to the lowest-DOF one, which is right at a tangency — a face on both
+/// a cylinder and its fillet torus is the cylinder's — but wrong when the
+/// simpler claimant is merely a *piece* of the more complex one: a cone fitted
+/// to one facet band of a torus is exact on that band (two coaxial circles
+/// always lie on a cone, SURFACE_FITTING.md "Option C"), and it would carve the
+/// band out of the fillet. A cylinder is never wholly inside its fillet — it
+/// continues past the junction rows the torus can reach — so the tangency rule
+/// is untouched; an impostor confined to one band is wholly inside the surface
+/// once that surface grows across the band from a seed of its own.
+///
+/// Computed over the whole committed set at once, so it does not depend on the
+/// order hypotheses were committed in; and it adds no constant — the bar is the
+/// vertex tolerance per-face resolution already uses.
+fn contained_hypotheses(
+    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
+    committed: &[CompeteHyp],
+    claim_lists: &[Vec<usize>],
+    hyp_area: &[f64],
+    vtol: f64,
+) -> Vec<(bool, usize)> {
+    (0..committed.len())
+        .map(|ci| {
+            let faces = committed[ci].faces();
+            let Some(&first) = faces.first() else { return (false, ci) };
+            claim_lists[first]
+                .iter()
+                .copied()
+                .filter(|&cj| cj != ci && hyp_area[cj] > hyp_area[ci])
+                .find(|&cj| {
+                    faces.iter().all(|&fi| {
+                        claim_lists[fi].contains(&cj) && max_vertex_dist(mesh, &committed[cj], fi) <= vtol
+                    })
```
